rendered: The premise is reversed: the low-Mn sample delivered more capacity, and the high-Mn sample delivered less. The low-Mn LNO gave 212 mAh g^− 1[1] of discharge capacity, versus 164 mAh g^− 1[2] for the high-Mn sample. In the thermal tests the high-Mn sample also released less heat, not more. The low-Mn sample released 901.4 J g^−1[3] during thermal decomposition, while the high-Mn sample released 485.7 J g^−1[4]. The high-Mn sample therefore released less heat, by 415.7[5] J per gram (the low-Mn value minus the high-Mn value). The high-Mn sample did not release more heat than the low-Mn sample.
